sites.name: Lake Albany clay plain
sites.notes: Glacial Lake Albany left thick clay deposits across the Albany area. Approximate area only; construction cuts and creek banks are often private.

sites.name: Garvies Point clay cliffs
sites.notes: Cretaceous clay exposed in shoreline bluffs on Long Island. This is a county preserve and museum, where removing material is normally not allowed. Listed for geology only; check the rules before visiting.

sites.name: Kerhonkson quadrangle (surficial map)
sites.notes: NYS Museum surficial geology sheet that describes glacial lake deposits. Glacial lake deposits mapped by the New York State Museum. A map sheet shows where lake-bed clay was laid down; it does not say the clay is accessible or legal to dig.

sites.name: Mohonk Lake quadrangle (surficial map)
sites.notes: NYS Museum sheet describing laminated silt and clay deposited in a glacial lake, roughly 3 to 15 meters thick. Glacial lake deposits mapped by the New York State Museum. A map sheet shows where lake-bed clay was laid down; it does not say the clay is accessible or legal to dig.

sites.name: Stony Clove Creek (Catskills)
sites.notes: Catskill stream management plans for Stony Clove note severe stream bank erosion and clay exposures along some banks. Approximate area. Banks are mostly private, and Forest Preserve land forbids removing soil.

sites.name: Champlain Valley lowlands
sites.notes: Champlain Sea and glacial lake clays fill the valley lowlands. Broad lowland area where glacial lakes or the Champlain Sea left clay. Not a collecting spot: use the soil explorer to look along streams here and ask landowners.

sites.name: St. Lawrence lowlands
